newsitem.title: FRANCE: SIDO cuts French soybean crushings, import targets.
newsitem.headline: SIDO cuts French soybean crushings, import targets.

text.p: The French oilseeds and protein seeds association SIDO on Tuesday cut its estimate for 1996/97 soybean crushings, citing competition from sunflower seeds and a firm dollar.
In its March report SIDO revised its target for soybean crushings to 570,000 tonnes from a January target of 600,000 and 512,000 tonnes in 1995/96.

"The monthly pace of soybean crushings should slow down at the end of the campaign from 55,000 tonnes to 35,000 tonnes -- sunflower (crushings) margins have become more favourable and the value of the dollar remains sustained," SIDO said.
SIDO also cut its estimate for soybean imports to 720,000 tonnes from a January target of 750,000 and 590,000 tonnes achieved in 1995/96.
It kept its estimate for the 1996 soybean crop unchanged at 240,000 tonnes. This would represent a fall of eight percent over 1995.
It also held its estimate for carryover stocks at end-June 1997 unchanged from January at 51,000 tonnes. This would compare with a carryover of 31,000 tonnes at end-June 1996.
